solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Car bullies nip to when out for spin (6,9)

indicatorNotes.out: letters that are out are knocked out of their order

annotation.surface: Some motoring thugs dash off for a quick drive.
annotation.walkthrough: "Spin" looks like a joyride, but here it is the noun for a slanted version of events, the trade of press officers.
annotation.definitionFit: Spin is the art of managing public opinion, which is what public relations people do.

entries.clue: Quiet individual in red, say (5)

blocks.note: someone in the red owes money: an ower

annotation.surface: Someone murmurs about a quiet person dressed in red.
annotation.walkthrough: "Say" looks like the usual 'for example' tag, but it is the noun: to have a say is to have power over a decision.
annotation.definitionFit: Say is used in its noun sense of influence over a decision, a near synonym.

entries.clue: Everyone has issue with British writer (9)

blocks.note: an issue under discussion is a point

annotation.surface: A British author is at odds with the whole world.
annotation.walkthrough: The "writer" is not an author but a pen.
annotation.definitionFit: A ballpoint is a pen, something you write with.

entries.clue: Knight one recalled as a bit of a looker (4)

indicatorNotes.recalled: called back, so the letters run backwards

annotation.surface: A knight is remembered as rather handsome.
annotation.walkthrough: "A looker" suggests an attractive person; here it is an eye, and the iris is a part of it.
annotation.definitionFit: The iris is part of the eye, the organ that looks.

entries.clue: Cattle poisoner in paper with men to get time (7)

blocks.note: a rag is a downmarket newspaper
other ranks: soldiers who are not officers

annotation.surface: A newspaper story about a cattle poisoner who gets a prison term.
annotation.walkthrough: Ragwort is a yellow-flowered weed that is toxic to livestock.
annotation.definitionFit: Ragwort poisons cattle and horses that eat it.

entries.clue: Regrets fast times being over in the morning (7)

indicatorNotes.being over: the fasts sit over, so around, the morning

blocks.note: Lent is a fast; several of them are Lents

annotation.surface: Someone rues staying up late until the early hours.
annotation.walkthrough: "Fast times" reads as wild living; it means periods of fasting.
annotation.definitionFit: To lament something is to regret it.

entries.clue: Extremely thuggish cur seizing larynx primarily? (9)

annotation.definition: Extremely thuggish cur seizing larynx primarily?

indicatorNotes.Extremely: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters
indicatorNotes.seizing: the rotter grabs the letter and holds it inside
indicatorNotes.primarily: first of all, so the opening letter

blocks.note: first and last letters of thuggish
a cur is a contemptible man, a rotter

annotation.surface: A brutish villain grabs someone by the throat.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and a description of the answer: a thug who seizes the larynx is a throttler.
annotation.definitionFit: A throttler strangles, gripping the throat where the larynx is.

entries.clue: Yellowy-orange line one mustn’t cross banking river (5)

indicatorNotes.banking: the line holds the river as a bank holds its money

blocks.note: the oche is the line a darts player must stand behind

annotation.surface: A painted line by a river that nobody may step over.
annotation.walkthrough: The oche is the throwing line in darts, a pub game popular in Britain.
annotation.definitionFit: Ochre is an earthy yellow-orange pigment and colour.

entries.clue: Developing harms last low-lying wetland (4,5)

annotation.surface: Building on a low-lying wetland does lasting damage.
annotation.walkthrough: A salt marsh is coastal land flooded by the tide.
annotation.definitionFit: A salt marsh is low-lying ground regularly soaked by seawater.

entries.clue: Welsh wicked at home, having good game (7)

blocks.note: ill as in evil, ill will

annotation.surface: A Welsh team plays badly at home but has a good match.
annotation.walkthrough: "Game" looks like a match; it is the adjective, as in 'game for anything'.
annotation.definitionFit: Game is the informal adjective for eager to take part, a plain synonym.

entries.clue: First of howitzers coming in alarms new officer (7)

indicatorNotes.First of: the first letter of the next word
indicatorNotes.coming in: the letter enters the other word
indicatorNotes.new: the letters are made new, into a fresh order

annotation.surface: A new officer is startled by incoming artillery fire.
annotation.walkthrough: "Alarms" reads as a verb in the surface, but it is the anagram fodder; "new officer" hides that "new" belongs to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A marshal is a high-ranking military or police officer.

entries.clue: Spending grand on beef can be excessive (4)

indicatorNotes.Spending: money spent is gone, so the grand is removed

blocks.note: a beef is a complaint, a gripe
a grand is a thousand pounds, G

annotation.surface: Paying a thousand for a cut of beef is too much.
annotation.walkthrough: "Beef" is a grumble, not meat, and a grand (£1,000) is G; language called a bit ripe is over the top.
annotation.definitionFit: Ripe can mean coarse or overdone, as in a ripe remark, which is excessive.

entries.clue: A worm tends to go with the flow (10)

indicatorNotes.to go: the letters go off into a new order

annotation.surface: An earthworm likes to follow the easy course.
annotation.walkthrough: "Tends" looks like part of the sentence's verb, but it is fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Going downstream is travelling with the current.

entries.clue: Reportedly do this to slow nag or dog (7)

indicatorNotes.Reportedly: as reported, so as it is spoken

blocks.note: a jockey whips a slow horse

annotation.surface: Advice on what to do with a lazy horse, or a dog.
annotation.walkthrough: A nag is a worn-out horse; say "whip it" and you hear the racing dog.
annotation.definitionFit: The whippet is a slim, fast dog bred for racing.

entries.clue: Deliberately annoying ending (7-2)

blocks.note: to wind someone up is to tease them on purpose
closing down a meeting or a company

annotation.surface: A finale meant to irritate.
annotation.walkthrough: Wind someone up is British for teasing or provoking them deliberately.
annotation.definitionFit: Winding up is both teasing someone on purpose and bringing something to a close.

entries.clue: Meander around with other posers at front? (9)

annotation.definition: Meander around with other posers at front?

indicatorNotes.at front: the fronts of the words, their first letters

blocks.note: used as it stands, for the mix
first letters of other and posers

annotation.surface: Showing off with fellow posers along the seafront.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the answer too: to promenade is to stroll the front, the seafront, being seen.
annotation.definitionFit: To promenade is to stroll in a leisurely way, often along a seafront promenade.

entries.clue: Bright yellow ruined plush fur female binned (7)

indicatorNotes.ruined: ruined things are wrecked into a new shape
indicatorNotes.binned: thrown away, so the letter is removed

annotation.surface: A garish yellow fur coat, spoilt and thrown out by a woman.
annotation.walkthrough: Take the F out of PLUSH FUR and rearrange what is left.
annotation.definitionFit: Sulphur is a pale bright yellow, named for the element.

entries.clue: Thumb your way through Amsterdam? (9)

blocks.note: not leafing through a guidebook but holding out a thumb for lifts
just an example destination, hence the question mark

annotation.surface: Finding your way around Amsterdam with your nose in a guidebook.
annotation.walkthrough: "Thumb your way through" suggests leafing through a book, like a city guide; hitchhikers thumb their way instead.
annotation.definitionFit: To hitchhike is to travel by thumbing lifts from passing drivers.

entries.clue: Thoughts and proposals lead to change for knight (7)

indicatorNotes.lead to change for: the leading letter is swapped for another

blocks.note: motions are proposals put to a meeting
N is the knight in chess notation, replacing M

annotation.surface: Ideas and suggestions that end in someone being knighted.
annotation.walkthrough: The lead letter M of MOTIONS gives way to N.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: ideas held in the mind.

entries.clue: Going down is what I do when working (7)

blocks.note: what the sun does in the evening
I is the crossword compiler, whose work is compiling puzzles

annotation.surface: Someone confesses they sink when they get to work.
annotation.walkthrough: "I" is the crossword setter speaking: a setter's work is setting puzzles.
annotation.definitionFit: The sun is setting as it goes down, and a setter at work is setting.

entries.clue: Small problem keeping Republican in nick (7)

indicatorNotes.keeping: the problem holds the letter inside

blocks.note: a hidden problem is a catch

annotation.surface: A minor issue: a Republican locked up in prison.
annotation.walkthrough: "Nick" looks like British slang for prison; here it is a small cut.
annotation.definitionFit: Nick in its sense of a small cut or mark on a surface is a plain synonym.

entries.clue: In which one on the blue might want to sink? (7)

annotation.definition: In which one on the blue might want to sink?

blocks.note: not a sailor at sea but a player whose next ball is the blue
not to go under but to pot the ball into a pocket

annotation.surface: Someone out on the open sea wishes to go under.
annotation.walkthrough: "On the blue" suggests at sea and "sink" drowning; in snooker, a player lining up the blue ball wants to sink it in a pocket.
annotation.definitionFit: Snooker is the cue game where coloured balls, including the blue, are sunk.

entries.clue: Piano featuring in popular piece for tour? (10)

indicatorNotes.featuring in: the piano appears inside the piece

blocks.note: a piece of something is a section
p is piano, soft in music

annotation.surface: A piano solo in a crowd-pleasing work on a concert tour.
annotation.walkthrough: The P sits inside SECTION, after its S.
annotation.definitionFit: A tour of inspection is a visit to look things over, as in a tour of the premises.

entries.clue: Standpoints of parties (5)

blocks.note: opposing groups in a dispute or match

annotation.surface: The positions taken by rival political parties.
annotation.walkthrough: Both halves mean the same word in slightly different senses.
annotation.definitionFit: A side is both a point of view and a group opposing another.

entries.clue: Second part of this appears in broadcast? (4)

indicatorNotes.Second part of: the second piece, here the second letter
indicatorNotes.appears in: the letter turns up inside the next word

blocks.note: to broadcast seed is to sow it

annotation.surface: A question about which part of a programme gets aired.
annotation.walkthrough: "Broadcast" works twice: scatter seed gives SOW, and a broadcast is a show.
annotation.definitionFit: As a noun, a broadcast is a programme put out on radio or television.

entries.clue: Comic performing in part of train (5)

annotation.surface: A comedian doing a set aboard a train.
annotation.walkthrough: In Britain a wagon is a railway goods truck.
annotation.definitionFit: A wagon is a single truck forming part of a freight train.

entries.clue: God is quietly unobtrusive, I hear (4)

indicatorNotes.I hear: what I hear is the sound, not the spelling

annotation.surface: A remark that a deity keeps a low profile.
annotation.walkthrough: Loki, the Norse trickster god, is anything but low-key, which is the joke.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the Norse trickster deity.

entries.clue: Old leader plus a fellow that soldier locks up (7)

indicatorNotes.locks up: the soldier holds the other letters inside

blocks.note: a GI is an American soldier

annotation.surface: A former ruler and a companion are jailed by a soldier.
annotation.walkthrough: Muammar Gaddafi ruled Libya until 2011.
annotation.definitionFit: Gaddafi was the long-time leader of Libya, now dead.

entries.clue: Wise man wrapping present (7)

indicatorNotes.wrapping: the man is wrapped around the present

blocks.note: the king is a man in chess

annotation.surface: One of the three wise men bringing a gift.
annotation.walkthrough: "Wise man" and "present" suggest the Magi with gifts; the definition is just "Wise", and "present" is time, not a gift.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: shrewd, showing understanding.

entries.clue: Old winger seeing gap’s prone to move (9,6)

indicatorNotes.to move: the letters move into a new order

annotation.surface: A veteran football winger spots space and is ready to run into it.
annotation.walkthrough: "Winger" suggests a footballer; it is a bird, and "old" because the passenger pigeon has been extinct since 1914.
annotation.definitionFit: The passenger pigeon is an extinct North American bird, an old winged creature.
